rationale: C13 is the strongest plausible template because it is the immediately preceding enlargement of the same monument and shares the same core drafting sequence: history and scientific justification, Antiquities Act authority, addition of federally owned or controlled lands, protection of valid existing rights, a warning against damage and settlement, and treatment of preexisting withdrawals and Alaska-specific claims. The child materially expands and adapts that machinery for a much larger addition, submerged lands and waters, water rights, subsistence uses, and later Alaska statutes. C14 and C18 contain additional close monument-enlargement formulas, especially future incorporation of nonfederal lands; C14 also parallels the child's dominant-reservation clause. Nevertheless, C13's same-monument continuity and Alaska-specific provisions make it the likeliest direct drafting source.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do proclaim that there are hereby set apart and reserved for inclusion in the Katmai National Monument all lands, including submerged lands, and waters owned or controlled by the United States within the boundaries
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do proclaim that, subject to valid existing rights, the lands owned or controlled by the United States within the following described boundary are hereby added to and made a part of the Katmai National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same operative framework to enlarge Katmai by designating federally owned or controlled property within a described boundary.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Section 2 of the Act of June 8, 1906 ... authorizes the President ... to declare by public proclamation ... objects of historic or scientific interest ... and to reserve as part thereof parcels of land ... confined to the smallest area compatible with the proper care and management
shared_material.parent_excerpt: under section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906 ... the President is authorized "to declare by public proclamation ... objects of historic or scientific interest ... and may reserve as a part thereof parcels of land ... confined to the smallest area compatible with the proper care and management"
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reproduces C13's statutory-authority recital and smallest-compatible-area formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Warning is hereby given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.
shared_material.explanation: This concluding warning is nearly verbatim and occupies the same late position in the proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The establishment of this addition is subject to valid existing rights ... Nothing in this Proclamation shall be deemed to revoke any existing withdrawal, reservation or appropriation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: subject to valid existing rights ... Any reservations or withdrawals heretofore made which affect the lands described above are hereby revoked.
shared_material.explanation: The child retains the same subjects—existing rights and prior withdrawals—but adapts the earlier machinery by preserving, rather than revoking, withdrawals under the later Alaska legal setting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: including ... valid selections under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act ... and under or confirmed in the Alaska Statehood Act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This proclamation shall not affect any claims ... of Alaska natives to the lands within the monument area.
shared_material.explanation: Both include Alaska-specific savings provisions protecting claims or selections associated with Native and state land rights.
